accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes a circular economy?
o: An economic system based primarily on the extraction and disposal of resources
An economic system based on increasing the use of fossil fuels
An economic system built on reuse, recycling and waste minimisation
An economic system focused exclusively on reducing carbon emissions
accepted.x: A circular economy is built on reuse, recycling and waste minimisation. It is not exclusively focused on carbon emissions or fossil fuels.
accepted.tq: Use the precise definition and reject the extreme word 'exclusively'.
accepted.sec: Circular economy - principles, linear vs circular, action plans  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding linear and circular economic models:
1. The linear model follows the sequence ‘take, make, dispose’.
2. In the circular model, materials are kept in use through reduction, reuse, repair and recycling.
3. In the linear model, waste becomes a resource and decouples growth from resource use.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because waste becoming a resource and decoupling growth from resource use are features of the circular model.
accepted.tq: Compare the defining sequences of the two models and find the reversed feature.
accepted.sec: Circular economy - principles, linear vs circular, action plans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In a circular economy, waste is viewed primarily as
o: a material that must always be incinerated
a source of greenhouse gases only
a resource that can be returned to productive use
accepted.x: The circular model treats waste as a resource, helping to decouple economic growth from resource use.
accepted.tq: Test the contrast between the linear endpoint and the circular resource approach.
accepted.sec: Circular economy - principles, linear vs circular, action plans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents priority waste streams for which circular-economy action plans were drawn up in India?
o: Coal, crude oil, natural gas, uranium and limestone
Food grains, cotton, jute, sugarcane and tea
Cement, glass, sand, clay and timber only
Plastics, e-waste, batteries, tyres and metals
accepted.x: NITI Aayog and MoEFCC committees drew up action plans for priority streams including plastics, e-waste, batteries, tyres and metals.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete named list rather than selecting a broader but unsupported group.
accepted.sec: Circular economy - principles, linear vs circular, action plans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about India’s Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks is correct?
o: They recycled 308 lakh tonnes of plastic, e-waste and batteries and generated 296.53 lakh tonnes of EPR certificates.
They recycled 308 crore tonnes of metals and generated 296.53 crore certificates.
They apply only to tyres and do not cover plastic or e-waste.
They recycled 296.53 lakh tonnes of waste and generated 308 lakh tonnes of certificates.
accepted.x: The EPR frameworks are reported to have recycled 308 lakh tonnes of plastic, e-waste and batteries and generated 296.53 lakh tonnes of EPR certificates.
accepted.tq: Split the paired figures and check both the unit and the relationship between recycling and certificates.

accepted.s: A green economy is best characterised by which one of the following?
o: Replacing all services with manufacturing activity
Decoupling growth from resource use and pollution while fostering green industries and jobs
Maximising economic growth through unrestricted resource extraction
Treating ecological scarcity as unrelated to economic development
accepted.x: A green economy reduces environmental risks and ecological scarcity, decouples growth from resource use and pollution, and fosters green industries and green jobs.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the full positive definition rather than an extreme substitute.
accepted.sec: Green economy and green technology - meaning, features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The green economy was a central theme of which event held in 2012?

accepted.s: Which of the following is included in the meaning of a green job?
o: Any work that increases the consumption of natural resources
Work in farming, industry, services or administration that preserves or restores environmental quality
Only government employment in forest departments
Only work directly related to renewable-energy generation
accepted.x: Green jobs may occur in farming, industry, services or administration and preserve or restore environmental quality.
accepted.tq: Watch for the restrictive word 'only' in the incorrect alternatives.
accepted.sec: Green economy and green technology - meaning, features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of green technology?
o: It recycles more of its waste.
It is necessarily inexpensive for developing countries.
accepted.x: High cost is a major barrier to green technology, particularly for developing countries; it is not necessarily inexpensive.
accepted.tq: Find the exception by separating core characteristics from the stated barrier.

accepted.s: Which of the following targets is associated with the European Green Deal?
o: A climate-neutral European Union by 2050 and at least a 55% greenhouse-gas reduction by 2030 from 1990 levels
A 55% reduction by 2050 compared with 2019 levels only
A climate-neutral European Union by 2030 and a 25% reduction by 2050
Net-zero emissions in all countries of the world by 2050
accepted.x: The European Green Deal aims at a climate-neutral EU by 2050 and at least a 55% reduction in greenhouse gases by 2030 compared with 1990.
accepted.tq: Check both the target year and the reference year before accepting the option.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding green chemistry:
1. It emphasises waste prevention rather than cleanup.
2. Atom economy is one of its principles.
3. It promotes safer solvents and reagents.
4. It supports energy-efficient processes and non-toxic, biodegradable products.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe principles or features included among the 12 Principles of Green Chemistry.
accepted.tq: Check whether each listed principle belongs to the same framework before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Green Chemistry and Cleaner Production - principles, link with EIA and LCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement best explains the relationship between green chemistry, cleaner production, EIA and LCA?
o: EIA and LCA are unrelated to sustainability and resource efficiency.
Cleaner production increases pollution so that LCA can measure it more accurately.
Green chemistry and cleaner production reduce waste and pollution across the product life cycle, thereby serving the goals of EIA and LCA.
Green chemistry deals only with final waste disposal, whereas EIA deals only with product marketing.
accepted.x: Green chemistry and cleaner production minimise waste and pollution and promote sustainability throughout the product life cycle, supporting the objectives of Environmental Impact Assessment and Life-Cycle Assessment.
accepted.tq: Trace the common life-cycle and sustainability link instead of treating the instruments as isolated concepts.
accepted.sec: Green Chemistry and Cleaner Production - principles, link with EIA and LCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Greenwashing refers to
o: the compulsory recycling of all industrial waste
making false or exaggerated claims that a product, firm or investment is environmentally friendly
the restoration of polluted water bodies through biological methods
the conversion of all investments into government securities
accepted.x: Greenwashing is the practice of making false or exaggerated environmental claims about a product, firm or investment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish misleading environmental communication from genuine environmental improvement.
accepted.sec: Greenwashing  [other exams]

accepted.s: Why is a clear taxonomy considered necessary in relation to greenwashing?
o: To replace life-cycle assessment with a single carbon figure
To help regulators curb greenwashing and transition washing
To remove all environmental regulations from financial markets
To classify only species threatened with extinction
accepted.x: A clear taxonomy helps regulators identify and curb greenwashing as well as transition washing.
accepted.tq: Identify the regulatory purpose of classification rather than its unrelated environmental uses.
